title: Large Language Models: A Survey
extended_summary:
This paper is a survey of large language models (LLMs), with a focus on major model families, training approaches, augmentation techniques, datasets, evaluation metrics, and benchmark performance. It is not an empirical study of an educational intervention, but rather a broad обзор of the LLM research landscape following the release of ChatGPT.

The paper reviews the development of LLMs from earlier statistical and neural language models through transformer-based pre-trained language models and into modern LLMs such as GPT, LLaMA, and PaLM. It summarizes key architectural choices, training stages such as pre-training, fine-tuning, instruction tuning, and alignment, and discusses how LLMs are used with external knowledge, tools, and agentic workflows.

No student population, school setting, or educational intervention is studied. The conclusions are conceptual: the paper argues that LLMs have rapidly expanded capabilities such as in-context learning, instruction following, reasoning, and tool use, while also noting ongoing challenges around efficiency, safety, ethics, and future model design. Because it is a survey, it does not report achievement outcomes, retention effects, or subgroup effects.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a narrative survey of large language models, not an empirical study of an educational intervention. It does not present a controlled methodology or primary outcome analysis relevant to K-12 mathematics achievement.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper has no measured educational impact and reports no effect sizes on student outcomes. It is background/overview literature rather than evidence of classroom or tutoring effects.
